reference.intent: Avoid false adjacent-lane/oncoming holds while maintaining continuous following. Source selected range uses centre/model-space extents and heading. CBE retains its exact padded affine world-frame hull and current velocity model, dead-hull observation and independent occupancy checks.

finding: Dense admission retained every moving hull, even when current vertical separation or an off-lane course below the existing crossing denominator cutoff meant neither braking branch could contribute. More than64 such candidates caused a density-only zero cap.
implementation: Reuse the existing crossing course/denominator before prediction-slot admission. Dense pruning requires finite own/other projected bounds and finite speed. Separate-height hulls and unoccupied slow/parallel courses below the existing0.2 denominator cutoff can be skipped; unknowns remain.

Current occupied-lane hulls and same-height crossing courses remain admitted. The exact existing crossing cutoff and both braking branches are unchanged. No new right-of-way, steering or height prediction is inferred.

More than256 raw hulls, more than64 retained candidates and scheduled direct calls above64 still refuse. Normal<=64 scenes retain the original constraint calculations. No new discovery query, ray, callback, timer, cache, controller or command.
cost: At most256 existing affine hull projections plus bounded finite/course arithmetic before up to64 full predictions. Course calculation reuses the existing velocity sample and is not repeated in crossing prediction. Discovery engine cost is unchanged; actual median/p95 impact remains unmeasured.
